CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up for chronic congestive heart failure with diastolic dysfunction and pre-operative clearance for knee surgery.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is a 77-year-old female with chronic congestive heart failure with diastolic dysfunction presenting for follow-up evaluation. She had an exacerbation of CHF in the spring with progressive dyspnea at which time her BNP was 3,000 in March and elevated to 6,000 in April. Her furosemide was switched to torsemide 20 mg daily and lisinopril was increased to 10 mg daily. Since these medication adjustments, patient reports significant symptomatic improvement with markedly improved dyspnea and urinary urgency. She notes that her current medication regimen including "oxyglutinine" has been helpful. She has experienced weight loss of approximately 3-3.5 pounds since her last visit in April. Recently she experienced bilateral leg cramps which she managed with approximately 4 ounces of pickle juice with good effect; she was counseled to use this in moderation due to salt content. She had previous episodes of heartburn which she treated with Prilosec for approximately 2 weeks in January; since discontinuing this medication, she has had no recurrence of heartburn symptoms. She is scheduled for right knee replacement surgery on June 24th and is being evaluated pre-operatively to optimize her cardiovascular status prior to surgery. She is overdue for colonoscopy screening.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Positive for resolved dyspnea with CHF exacerbation now improved, resolved recent bilateral leg cramps, resolved heartburn. Negative for current dyspnea, chest pain, fever. Uses bathroom appropriately with improved urgency. All other systems reviewed and negative.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Chronic congestive heart failure with diastolic dysfunction; history of anemia; diabetes mellitus; right knee osteoarthritis (scheduled for replacement).

MEDICATIONS
Torsemide 20 mg by mouth daily; Lisinopril 10 mg by mouth daily; Iron supplement daily; Clopidogrel (to be discontinued 1 week prior to surgery); Magnesium supplement 1 g twice daily recommended to initiate. Not currently on potassium supplement.

ALLERGIES
No known drug allergies documented.

FAMILY HISTORY
No family history of colon cancer. Other family history not documented.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient lives with husband. Has Medicare and private insurance through spouse's employment (spouse's insurance coverage may be ending). Patient demonstrates good compliance and organization with medical care, keeping medical information on her phone and posted reminders at bedside.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital Signs: Blood pressure good. General: Well-appearing, in no acute distress. Lungs: Clear to auscultation bilaterally with good air movement. Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm. Extremities: No edema noted.

RESULTS
Laboratory Results: Hemoglobin normal (prior anemia resolved); Potassium 3.9 mEq/L (stable on torsemide); Creatinine 0.7 mg/dL (normal, appropriate kidney function); BUN 23 mg/dL (slightly elevated, suggesting possible mild dehydration); Magnesium 1.7 mg/dL (normal but below optimal target of 2.0 range); Blood glucose 169 mg/dL (non-fasting); A1C 5.5% in March (or 5.1% per other documentation); BNP 3,000 in March, 6,000 in April, current results still pending. Imaging: Recent chest X-ray on file.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Chronic Congestive Heart Failure with Diastolic Dysfunction: Mixed presentation with prior exacerbation in spring. Medication adjustment from furosemide to torsemide 20 mg daily and lisinopril increased to 10 mg daily has resulted in good symptomatic response with improved dyspnea, non-labored breathing, and weight loss of 3-3.5 pounds. Lab work shows stable potassium and appropriate creatinine. Continue torsemide 20 mg daily and lisinopril 10 mg daily. Initiate magnesium supplement 1 g twice daily to optimize cardiac muscle stability (current magnesium 1.7, target 2.0 range). Repeat EKG today. Await current BNP results.

2. Pre-operative Evaluation for Right Knee Replacement: Surgery scheduled for June 24th at East Metro. Complete pre-operative check within 2 weeks of surgery (first or second week of June). EKG to be performed today. No additional chest X-ray needed. No additional blood work at this time but may need repeat A1C prior to surgery. Discontinue clopidogrel 1 week prior to surgery. Patient has written reminders and will receive clinic reminder.

3. Screening Colonoscopy: Patient is overdue for screening. Schedule within next 30 days to address patient's concerns regarding spouse's insurance coverage. Colonoscopy options include Dr. Martin at County Surgical Services or Valley Medical in Springfield. Completing colonoscopy will not delay knee surgery. No family history of colon cancer.

4. Diabetes Mellitus: A1C 5.5% in March. Blood glucose today 169 mg/dL (non-fasting). Continue current regimen. May repeat A1C prior to knee surgery.
